message.content:
I have the full kernel source and contract already loaded, so I'll analyze the implementation directly and record a structured description.

Key structural observations before recording: the Triton kernel maps query blocks via `qpos = qb*BQ + rows//GROUP` / `head = kv_head*GROUP + rows%GROUP` (matching the contiguous GQA head-grouping in `reference`); tile iteration is bounded by `max_prefix = min(context + qb*BQ + BQ, length)` which is provably ≤ (highest valid row's absolute position)+1; disallowed scores are set to `-inf` before the running max, which sanitizes NaN from out-of-window K tiles; and the window-mode V zeroing at line 70 keeps `logical ≥ first_key`, which is the union superset of per-row allowed windows (lowest `qpos` has the smallest lower bound), so it cannot under-count higher rows. The main residual uncertainties are precision-related (FP16 cast of probabilities before the V dot, FP16 output quantization vs the 0.003+0.003·|target| tolerance) and edge cases in the windowed tile-range arithmetic.

message.reasoning_content:
Analyze the kernel for bugs. Key suspicion: the sliding-window tile-range logic and masking.

Notable issues:
- Grouped heads: qpos = qb*BQ + rows//GROUP, head = kv_head*GROUP + rows%GROUP. BQ = 16//group. rows = 0..15. Fine.
- max_prefix = context + qb*BQ + BQ — this is one past the last absolute query position for this block. But qpos may exceed QT within a block when QT not divisible by BQ; masked by qpos<QT.
- WINDOW>0: tile range computed from first_key etc. But if qb*BQ + BQ > QT, last_key uses min(qb*BQ+BQ-1, QT-1) — ok.
- Critical: line 70, v masking uses qpos_lo = qb*BQ (the lowest qpos in block) instead of per-row qpos. For V, positions masked via scores to -inf; exp(-inf - max) = 0, so v doesn't actually need masking—unless... wait, probabilities = exp(scores - updated_max); -inf scores → 0 probabilities, so v value is multiplied by 0. But if v contains NaN/Inf in unreachable slots, 0*NaN = NaN in tl.dot! That's why they mask v: to avoid NaN contamination. The v masking at line 70 uses qpos_lo — only keeps v rows where (context + qpos_lo - logical) < WINDOW. Positions allowed for any query row in the block are those with logical > context+qpos_lo - WINDOW... Actually allowed set over the block is union: positions allowed for the highest qpos (largest set). Line 70 masks v to positions allowed for the LOWEST qpos — stricter. But stricter masking combined with probability 0 for positions not allowed... wait if v is set to 0 for a position allowed for a higher qpos, then accumulator gets p*0 = 0 for that position — undercounts! That's a bug: rows other than the lowest qpos lose contributions from positions between (context+qpos_lo-WINDOW, context+qpos-WINDOW). Hmm, check: for qpos > qpos_lo, allowed positions include logical > context+qpos-WINDOW, which is a larger lower bound... wait, allowed: absolute_q - logical < WINDOW → logical > absolute_q - WINDOW. Larger qpos → larger absolute_q → larger set of allowed logical (up to absolute_q). Line 70 keeps v only where context+qpos_lo - logical < WINDOW, i.e., logical > context+qpos_lo-WINDOW — that's the LARGEST set (lowest qpos has smallest absolute_q, so its allowed set lower bound is smallest). Wait absolute_q = context+qpos. allowed when absolute_q - logical < WINDOW → logical > absolute_q - WINDOW. For qpos_lo (smallest qpos), logical > context+qpos_lo-WINDOW — the most permissive mask. So line 70 masks v to the union superset — correct (keeps v for positions allowed for any row). Actually it keeps positions allowed by the lowest qpos, which is a superset of all others. Good — that's the union. So masking v is safe: probabilities already zero elsewhere, and NaN slots outside every allowed set are zeroed. Wait but is it the superset? For row with qpos, allowed lower bound logical > context+qpos-WINDOW. qpos_lo gives smallest bound → largest set. Yes superset. OK so line 70 is fine for avoiding NaN.

But: k load masked by tile_mask (logical < max_prefix), not by allowed set. k positions beyond max_prefix load other=0.0, fine. But k loaded for positions in tiles within [tile_start, tile_end) that include positions < first_key? tile_start floor-divides, so tile may contain positions earlier than first_key; scores masked to -inf there → fine, but k NaN? k loaded from table mapping — those are valid positions (< length, ceil covered by table), problem says only reachable slots must be finite; positions in [0, length) but outside window for all queries in this block... are they "reachable by at least one allowed position of at least one query in this call"? Only if some other query block reaches them. If a tile range includes positions not allowed for any query (e.g., positions before first_key of the last block), those cache slots may be arbitrary NaN — and k loads them, scores = SCALE*dot(q,k) = q·NaN = NaN, then tl.where(mask, scores, -inf) — where selects but NaN in the "true" branch... where(False, NaN, -inf) returns -inf, fine. But tl.max(scores) over the row could include NaN only if unselected? tl.where replaces first — scores already replaced with -inf at masked positions before max. Actually NaN at positions where the mask is True? The mask is (qpos<QT)&allowed&tile_mask — positions with k NaN but not allowed are masked out. Positions with k NaN but allowed → contract violation, can't happen. So scores NaN only at disallowed positions, replaced by -inf. OK.

But wait — the dot product q·k computed over the whole tile before masking: 0-masked... k other=0.0 for out-of-table; NaN entries at disallowed positions produce NaN scores which are then replaced. Fine.

Bigger issue: tile_start/tile_end when WINDOW>0 — computed per program (per qb block), and loop range is dynamic. In Triton, range with dynamic bounds OK.

Issue: WINDOW>0 and tile skipping: v masking line 70 uses qpos_lo but the allowed condition for scores uses per-row absolute_q — good.

Potential issue: when WINDOW > 0 and the block's tiles were entirely skipped... For a row whose allowed positions fall in tiles outside [tile_start, tile_end)? last_key = context + min(qb*BQ+BQ-1, QT-1) — the highest query row in the block. tile_end covers up to that. Rows within block have absolute positions ≤ that, fine. tile_start covers lowest qpos allowed set. Fine.

Issue: max_prefix uses qb*BQ+BQ, but valid rows only qpos<QT; masked by tile_mask — positions between length and max_prefix? max_prefix = min(context+qb*BQ+BQ, length), so ≤ length. Fine.

Issue: denominator initial 1.0 with maximum -inf; alpha = exp(-inf - max) → exp(-inf)=0? First tile: maximum=-inf, updated_maximum> -inf presumably, alpha = exp(-inf - finite) = 0, denominator = 1*0 + sum. OK. If all scores -inf in a tile (possible?), updated_maximum stays -inf → set to 0, probabilities = exp(-inf - 0) = 0, alpha = exp(-inf-0)=0 → accumulator*0, denominator*0. OK. Final: if no tiles at all (tile_start ≥ tile_end, e.g., WINDOW small and ... hmm), denominator stays 1.0, accumulator 0 → output 0. Reference: every query attends at least position a itself (t=a allowed). So denominators shouldn't be empty unless tile range empty incorrectly. Could tile_end ≤ tile_start when WINDOW>0? last_key ≥ context+qb*BQ ≥ ... last_key //TILE +1 ≥ ... and tile_start = max(0, first_key//TILE). If first_key is very negative, tile_start=0. Could first_key > last_key? first_key = context+qb*BQ-WINDOW+1, last_key = context+min(qb*BQ+BQ-1, QT-1). If WINDOW large (>BQ), first_key < last_key always. WINDOW ≥1: if WINDOW=1, first_key = context+qb*BQ, last_key ≥ context+qb*BQ → ok. Fine.

FP16 output tolerance: probabilities cast to v.dtype (fp16) before dot with fp16 v, accumulator fp32. Tolerance 0.003+0.003|target| relative-ish; fp16 rounding of probabilities ~6e-4 each; sum of up to 512 terms... error could exceed tolerance? error_ratio uses max over elements. Sum p_i rounding errors: each p*0.0005 absolute worst; sum of 512 with p summing 1 → up to 0.0005 absolute vs tolerance 0.003. Probably ok. Also output stored as FP16, quantization 0.001 at |x|~1, tolerance 0.003+0.003|.|. Marginal but likely fine.

Suspicion: `enable_fp_fusion=False` — prevents fma; fine.

Another: q loaded with mask qpos<QT, other=0.0; rows with qpos≥QT have q=0, scores computed =0, masked by qpos<QT in where → -inf. Good. Store masked. Good.

K layout: k physical [P,S,HK,D], base = ((physical*PAGE + logical%PAGE)*HK + kv_head)*D. Matches. But qo uses head = kv_head*GROUP + rows%GROUP — assumes q heads grouped contiguously (head h uses kv head h//GROUP), consistent with reference head_map = arange(hq)//(hq//hk). Good.

Potential issue: int32 overflow? physical*PAGE*HK*D max 256*64*4*128 = 8.4M — ok in int32, but .to(int64) anyway.

TILE=64 fixed, but PAGE can be 16 or 32: logical//PAGE — page boundaries within a tile handled per-token, fine. TABLE_WIDTH load: batch*TABLE_WIDTH + logical//PAGE; logical//PAGE could exceed TABLE_WIDTH-1 when logical near max_prefix but < length; ceil(length/page) ≤ C, so logical//PAGE ≤ ceil(length/page)-1 < C. Fine (tile_mask bounds logical < max_prefix ≤ length).

Wait, one more: when WINDOW>0, tile_mask is logical < max_prefix where max_prefix based on block's max; for rows... fine.

The real risk I should flag for Skeptic: (1) FP16 precision (probabilities.to(fp16) and dot in fp16) vs 0.003 tolerance, especially with D=128, long contexts; (2) the v window mask at line 70 correctness (superset argument); (3) tile-range window logic edge cases (WINDOW≥TILE, qt>BQ remainder); (4) NaN in unreachable cache slots loaded by k within tiles (masked to -inf — but does tl.where fully sanitize? scores = SCALE*dot; dot of fp16 with NaN yields NaN; where replaces with -inf only where condition false; condition true & NaN impossible by contract); (5) v loaded with mask=tile_mask — positions ≥ max_prefix get other=0, but positions < max_prefix not allowed for any row still loaded as NaN, then zeroed at line 70 (window case). In non-window case (WINDOW=0), line 70 not executed! Then v NaN at positions allowed for some row? If allowed for some row, contract says finite. Positions < max_prefix but > absolute_q for a row → that row's probability is 0 but dot(probabilities, v) computes 0*NaN = NaN. Are such positions allowed for at least one query in the call? max_prefix = context + qb*BQ + BQ (clamped to length); highest query in block has absolute position min(context+qb*BQ+BQ-1, length-1)... wait a = context + qpos, qpos ≤ QT-1, so a ≤ context+QT-1 = length-1. max_prefix = min(context+qb*BQ+BQ, length). For the last block, qb*BQ+BQ ≥ QT possibly > QT, so max_prefix = length. Positions between a_max+1 and length-1... a_max for last block = length-1, so all positions < length are ≤ some a. But for non-final blocks, max_prefix = context+qb*BQ+BQ = a_max+1 where a_max = context+qb*BQ+BQ-1 (if within QT). So tile_mask logical < max_prefix ⇒ logical ≤ a_max — allowed for the highest row. So every loaded v position is allowed for at least one query row in the block → finite per contract... but only if that row is valid (qpos < QT). If block's highest qpos ≥ QT (last partial block), max_prefix clamped to length — position ≤ length-1 ≤ context+QT-1 = a of last row. OK. So non-window: no NaN risk in v. And k similarly masked by tile_mask: positions < max_prefix ≤ allowed for top row. Hmm, but only when that top row is in this block... yes a_max is a row of this block.

But wait — when WINDOW>0: tiles [tile_start, tile_end) may include positions not allowed for any row of the block (e.g., between tile_start*64 and first_key). Those k values may be NaN (reachable? by other blocks maybe, but "at least one query in this call" — earlier blocks with lower qpos have lower a... actually a increases with qpos; earlier blocks have smaller a, so positions near first_key of a later block ARE allowed for earlier-block rows? first_key of block = a_lo - WINDOW + 1; earlier rows have smaller a so allowed positions are even earlier — position between tile_start*TILE and first_key might not be allowed for anyone if window small... position p < first_key: p < a_lo - WINDOW + 1, so a_lo - p ≥ WINDOW, not allowed for a_lo; for smaller a, a - p even larger → not allowed. So those positions can hold NaN k. Loaded → scores NaN → where → -inf. OK sanitized. v: those positions → line 70 masks them to 0 (context+qpos_lo - logical ≥ WINDOW ⇒ zeroed; first_key-1 = context+qpos_lo-WINDOW, so positions ≤ first_key-1 are zeroed... condition (context+qpos_lo - logical) < WINDOW keeps logical > context+qpos_lo-WINDOW = first_key-1, i.e., logical ≥ first_key). And allowed rows require logical ≥ a-WINDOW+1 ≥ context+qpos_lo-WINDOW+1. So kept set = logical ≥ first_key ⊇ all allowed. Good, so v NaN positions below first_key zeroed. Positions ≥ max_prefix: masked at load (other=0). So line 70 handles window NaN correctly. And in non-window, k/v loads limited to tile_mask < max_prefix ≤ allowed for top row. Actually wait, is max_prefix ≤ a_max+1 always? max_prefix = min(context+qb*BQ+BQ, length). If qb*BQ+BQ > QT, and context+qb*BQ+BQ < length? Possible: context = length-QT, context+qb*BQ+BQ where qb*BQ+BQ could exceed QT only for last block; context + (qb*BQ+BQ) where qb*BQ+BQ ≤ QT+15... e.g., QT=33, BQ=16, last qb=2, qb*BQ+BQ=48 > 33. context+48 vs length = context+33 → min picks length. So max_prefix ≤ length = context+QT = a_max+1. Good.

So kernel seems largely correct. Remaining risk: precision (fp16 dot of probabilities·v and q·k in fp16 vs FP64 reference, tolerance 0.003 relative — D=128, values ±1, dot q·k error ~ sqrt(128)*2^-11 ≈ 0.055 in raw score... scores ~ SCALE*dot; SCALE=1/sqrt(128)~0.088, error ~0.005 in score — affects softmax slightly. tolerance is on output 0.003+0.003|target|. Might be borderline. That's the main Skeptic surface.

Also q·k via tl.dot with fp16 inputs and fp32 accumulate: Triton dot fp16→fp32, error per product fp16 rounding 2^-11 relative... inputs exact fp16, accumulate fp32, so dot is quite accurate actually (products exact? fp16*fp16 exact in fp32, accumulation fp32). Good. The main lossy step: probabilities.to(v.dtype) → fp16 rounding of p (up to 2^-11 relative). Output error ≤ sum |p|*2^-11*|v| ≈ 2^-11 ≈ 5e-4, well within 0.003. Fine.

Also store: result fp32 → OUT fp16 conversion, rounding 2^-11 relative — within tolerance.

One more: `maximum` initialization with denominator=1.0 and the "no allowed positions in a processed tile but tiles processed" case — handled. What if tile loop empty for a valid row? Row a always allows position a = context+qpos ∈ tiles up to a//TILE. tile_end = min(last_key//TILE+1, num_tiles). last_key ≥ context+qb*BQ ≥ context+qpos = a for all rows in the block? last_key = context + min(qb*BQ+BQ-1, QT-1) ≥ context+qpos since qpos ≤ QT-1 and qpos ≤ qb*BQ+BQ-1 (qpos = qb*BQ+rows//GROUP < qb*BQ+BQ). Yes. So a's tile covered. Good.

Also — `length` loaded as int32, context could be negative? length ≥ QT per contract, so context ≥ 0. OK.

Risk worth noting: negative context never happens. QT up to 33, BQ = 16//group; if group=8 (hq/hk=8, hq up to 16), BQ=2; if group... group ∈{1,2,4,8}, BQ ∈ {16,8,4,2}. BM=16 rows, rows//GROUP covers BQ positions × GROUP heads = 16. Good.

Edge: WINDOW > 0 but window > context, first_key negative → tile_start=0 fine.

I'll record the description update.
